DEQUEUE(Q)
Type: Algorithm
Steps: (1) x = Q[Q.head] (2) if Q.head == Q.size → Q.head = 1 else
Q.head = Q.head + 1 (3) return x

messages.content:
This is a **DEQUEUE** operation on a queue implemented as a **circular array** (likely from Ch. 10 — Elementary Data Structures).

**How it works:**

1. **`x = Q[Q.head]`** — Read the element at the front of the queue (position tracked by `Q.head`).

2. **Advance the head pointer** — If `Q.head` is at the last index of the array (`Q.size`), wrap around to position 1. Otherwise, increment by 1. This is the "circular" behavior — the array logically loops around, so you don't shift elements.

3. **`return x`** — Return the dequeued element.

**Key details from the surrounding context (likely Ch. 10):**

- A queue is FIFO (first-in, first-out).
- `Q.head` indexes the front element; `Q.tail` indexes the next free slot.
- The queue is empty when `Q.head == Q.tail`. The wrapped-around branch prevents the head from running past the physical array bounds.
- Underflow condition: you must check `Q.head == Q.tail` before calling DEQUEUE (not shown in this snippet).
- All operations are O(1).

**The conditional** `if Q.head == Q.size` handles the wrap-around for the circular implementation — if head was at the last slot, it resets to 1 rather than going out of bounds.
